CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to review symptom logs since the last appointment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, bringing updated symptom logs and medication response records for the past month. He reports continued stability in his anxiety levels, noting that the cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) sessions have been beneficial, particularly in managing situational anxiety related to public speaking. He expresses appreciation for the strategies learned during therapy, which he utilizes during high-pressure situations.
In terms of insomnia, Mr. Smith states that trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime remains effective for sleep initiation but nocturnal awakenings persist, averaging three to four times per night. He reports that melatonin at 10 mg has not significantly altered his sleep architecture, although he feels it may contribute slightly to overall sleep quality. He continues to wake feeling fatigued, which he attributes to these disturbances.
His tension-type headaches have maintained a frequency of approximately twice weekly, with a moderate intensity rated at 4 to 6 out of 10 on the pain scale. He continues to use ibuprofen 600 mg as needed, which provides satisfactory relief. Mr. Smith expresses interest in exploring preventive options, particularly non-pharmacological interventions, to further reduce the frequency of headache episodes.
Mr. Smith acknowledges persistent fatigue, which he feels is exacerbated by both his sleep issues and work-related stress. He reports that bupropion at 150 mg daily has provided some stabilization of his energy levels, but he continues to experience afternoon lethargy and occasional difficulty concentrating.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 6. Lorazepam 1 mg twice daily as needed (continued) 7. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 8. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 9. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith maintains a balanced lifestyle, engaging in regular physical activity, including yoga and brisk walking. He has successfully reduced his caffeine intake and continues to practice mindfulness techniques, although he reports that work stress occasionally disrupts his routine.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety remains stable; sleep quality is a persistent concern; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity rated as moderate; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, with some variations; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/80 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears fatigued but engaged; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Maintain CBT sessions; assess progress at the next visit. Lorazepam at 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety will remain on the regimen. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime. Given the ongoing nocturnal awakenings, consider increasing melatonin to 20 mg if sleep quality does not improve in the next month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. Discuss referral to a neurologist for evaluation of preventive therapies if headache frequency or intensity does not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage regular exercise and stress management techniques. Re-evaluate fatigue levels and consider additional interventions if there is no improvement by the next appointment.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-07-01 to continue monitoring symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain a detailed log of his symptoms, medication responses, and any potential triggers for his anxiety or headaches to facilitate ongoing management.
